- Model consistently underestimates early spikes (e.g., 47.00, 49.61) and overestimates late declines (e.g., 35.94, 33.75) — adjust for lagged reaction to policy or supply shocks.
- Forecast mean is too low relative to true mean — increase baseline by 2–3% for 30-day horizon.
- After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 5–7 days post-spike.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true volatility — increase standard deviation by 15–20% for high-variance periods (e.g., post-2023-08-16).
